context.scope: incoming order management by email + invoicing

processes.name: Email triage and qualification
processes.trigger: Opening Gmail inbox in the morning (~8:00am)
steps: Log into Gmail
Read 10 to 40 new emails
Visually identify order emails (subject + reading the body)
Separate: orders vs customer questions vs supplier emails
processes.output: Mental list of emails to process as orders
pain_points: No Gmail filter — everything is mixed together
Some order emails don't have 'Order' in the subject

processes.name: Order entry
steps: Read the full email to extract: customer name, email, product(s), quantity/quantities, shipping address
Quick stock check in the Stock tab of the Google Sheet
Open Google Sheet 'Orders'
Manual entry: date, name, email, product, quantity, address, status='New'
Assign an order number (last number + 1)
pain_points: 30% of emails are missing the shipping address — requires a customer follow-up
Stock not always up to date at time of check
Order number incremented manually — risk of error or duplicate

processes.name: Order confirmation email
processes.trigger: Order logged in P02 (if stock available)
steps: Open confirmation draft in Gmail
Personalise: first name, product, quantity, amount, estimated delay, order number
Send to customer
pain_points: Risk of forgetting if Marc is interrupted between P02 and P03
Manual personalisation every time despite a fixed template
No record of the send in Google Sheets

processes.name: Out-of-stock management
processes.trigger: Stock outage discovered (during P02 or during fulfilment by Julien)
steps: Detect the outage (late: often 1–2 days after the order)
Call or email the customer to apologise and offer: restock delay, substitute product, or refund
Wait for customer response
Update status in Google Sheets
If refund: process refund manually
processes.output: Order cancelled or rescheduled; customer notified
pain_points: Late detection (confirmation already sent to customer)
Degraded customer experience: received a confirmation then a cancellation
Significant time: 45 min average per incident
Loss of loyal customers estimated by Marc

processes.name: Weekly invoicing
steps: Open Google Sheet 'Orders', filter on current week
For each order: open Word template
Enter information: customer name, address, products, amounts, invoice number
Export to PDF via Acrobat Reader
Send by email to customer
Update the Excel numbering table
pain_points: 2 hours every Friday — purely repetitive task
Risk of errors on amounts or addresses (generates credit notes)
No dedicated software: fragile and non-scalable workflow
No automatic numbering — risk of gaps or duplicates

pain_points_summary.description: 30 min/day of copy-paste to log email orders
Missed or delayed confirmations when interrupted
Stock outages discovered late — crisis management 45 min × 2–3/month
2h of manual invoicing every Friday — not scalable
30% of email orders are missing the address — customer follow-up required

systems.name: PrestaShop
systems.note: Handles online orders — out of scope for this pipeline

unclear_areas: Exact format of order email bodies (too variable to guarantee automatic extraction without testing on real emails)
Volume of phone/SMS orders (not quantified — out of scope for V1)
Stock reorder threshold (Delphine manages manually — out of scope for V1)
